cms.title: Dinara Safina ended the hopes of two home players, Zheng Jie in the third round and Li Na in the semifinals, as well as defeating No.2 seed Jelena Jankovic in the quarterfinals, en route to capturing silver at Beijing 2008.

Yan Zi and Zheng Jie won a marathon quarterfinal 6-3, 5-7, 10-8 over top seeds Svetlana Kuznetsova and Dinara Safina, then beat Alona and Kateryna Bondarenko 6-2, 6-2 to win the bronze play-off in front of the Chinese duo's home crowd at Beijing 2008.

A 17-year-old Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova stunned World No.3 Jelena Jankovic 6-4, 6-4 in the second round of Indian Wells 2009, going on to claim a second Top 10 scalp in Agnieszka Radwanska to make her maiden semifinal.
Kim Clijsters, Georgina Clark, Adam Barrett - 2003 Miami
cms.description: Kim Clijsters (center) received the Sportsmanship Award eight times, pictured here in 2003 with WTA Legend Georgina Clark and Miami tournament director Adam Barrett.

cms.title: Belgium’s Kim Clijsters beat Maria Sharapova, 6-3, 7-5 to take the 2005 Miami crown.
After a nine-year absence from the Miami final, Venus returned in 2010 with wins over Agnieszka Radwanska and Marion Bartoli - but fell 6-2, 6-1 to Kim Clijsters at the last hurdle (Getty)

Kim Clijsters completed a remarkable Sunshine Double in 2005 on her return from a wrist injury, becoming the lowest-ranked (at World No.38) and first unseeded player to win the Miami title with a 6-3, 7-5 win over Maria Sharapova in the final (Getty)

Kim Clijsters took her second Miami trophy in 2010, dethroning Victoria Azarenka 6-4, 6-0 in round four, edging Justine Henin 6-2, 6-7(3), 7-6(6) in the SFs and capturing her third post-maternity title 6-2, 6-1 over Venus Williams in the final (Getty)

Australian Open winner Kenin's loss to Azarenka was just the second time in the Open Era that a reigning Grand Slam champion had been double bagelled, following Maria Sharapova's loss to Lindsay Davenport at Indian Wells 2005.
Jelena Jankovic has gone very far in Miami before - she was runner-up to Serena Williams in 2008.
Serena Williams claimed glory in 2013 with a 4–6, 6–3, 6–0 victory in the Miami final over Maria Sharapova. It was Williams' sixth Miami title.
In 2014, Serena Williams defeated Li Na to claim the second leg of her second hat-trick of Miami titles (Getty)

Serena Williams's fifth Miami title in 2008 was her toughest yet, and saw her battle through three-setters against Flavia Pennetta in the third round, Svetlana Kuznetsova in the semifinals and Jelena Jankovic 6-1, 5-7, 6-3 in the final (Getty)
Agnieszka Radwanska won her biggest title yet at Miami 2013 without dropping a set, including wins over Garbiñe Muguruza, Venus Williams and Maria Sharapova 7-5, 6-4 in the final (Getty)
Vera Zvonareva - Indian Wells 125 2020 - Oracle Challenger Series
No.1 seed and 2015 Dubai champion Simona Halep thrilled her Romanian supporters in the U.A.E. with a come-from-behind quarterfinal victory over No.7 seed Aryna Sabalenka.
cms.subtitle: Simona Halep - 2020 Dubai - Getty

cms.title: 2011 saw Halep begin to threaten big names, taking her first Top 20 scalp in Toronto over Svetlana Kuznetsova and her first Top 10 win in a 6-2, 7-5 first-round upset of Li Na at the US Open - cracking the Top 50 as a result.

In the first round of the 2011 US Open, Simona Halep shocked reigning Roland Garros champion Li Na 6-2, 7-5 for her first Top 10 win - two weeks after scoring her first Top 20 win over Svetlana Kuznetsova in Toronto - and cracked the Top 50 as a result.
Doha 2008 was the scene of the first meeting between Maria Sharapova and Caroline Wozniacki, with the former winning, 6-0, 6-1. (Getty)
That win would spur Kvitova on to two more victories that week, and she claimed her first title of 2016 in Wuhan. (Getty Images)
The pair would meet once more in 2016, on the hardcourts of Wuhan, where Kvitova prevailed 6-3, 6-4 in the quarterfinals. (Getty Images)
Petra Kvitova won the inaugural Wuhan Open in 2014 by overcoming Eugenie Bouchard, 6-3, 6-4. She did not lose a set all week. (Getty)
Petra Kvitova won her first encounter with Caroline Garcia 6-3, 6-4 in the 2014 Wuhan quarterfinals on the way to her third title of that year (Getty)
Paula Badosa Team 2021 WTA Finals Guadalajara
But she won eight of her last nine matches of 2014, the semis in Beijing and a title in Osaka.

In 2011, an injury sustained in Canada forced Kim Clijsters to withdraw from the US Open as the defending champion for the second time - this time an abdominal issue suffered in the second round of Toronto against Zheng Jie (Getty)

Beijing champion Caroline Garcia has become the first woman since Victoria Azarenka's 2016 Sunshine Double to win back-to-back Premiers - and, on an 11-match winning streak, has been unstoppable in Asia (Getty)

Beijing champion Caroline Garcia has become the first woman since Victoria Azarenka's 2016 Sunshine Double to win back-to-back Premiers - and, on an 11-match winning streak, has been unstoppable in Asia (Getty)

Serena Williams continued to stamp her ownership of Miami on the tournament with a seventh crown in 2014, dropping one set to Caroline Garcia in the third round and beating Li Na 7-5, 6-1 in the final (Getty)
Caroline Wozniacki celebrates returning to World No.1 with a beautiful floral display during day five of the Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships in February 2011 (Getty)
Caroline Wozniacki's sixth and most recent successful title defence came at Tokyo in 2017 with a win over Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova in the final (Getty)
Osaka made her first final at Tokyo 2016, beating Elina Svitolina and falling to Caroline Wozniacki - a run that saw the Japanese player break the Top 50 (Getty)

Schiavone would reach three more finals in 2005, including her first at Tier I level in Moscow, where she beat Amélie Mauresmo, Svetlana Kuznetsova and Elena Dementieva before falling to Mary Pierce (Getty)
Former World No.1 Garbiñe Muguruza will return to the WTA Finals for the first time since 2017. The Spaniard won titles in Dubai and Chicago this year.
Jelena Jankovic claimed the Kremlin Cup in Moscow to win her third title in as many weeks as she stormed to the top of the charts in the fall of 2008.
In 2001, Jennifer Capriati clinched the crown in Charleston before collecting her second Grand Slam title of the season at Roland Garros.

Future Roland Garros legend Justine Henin was a title favorite in 2002 after winning Berlin - but the No.5 seed crashed out 4-6, 6-1, 6-0 to Hungary's Aniko Kapros, an 18-year-old No.179-ranked qualifier, in the first round.

Victoria Jimenez Kasintseva, 15, became the first ever Andorran to play in a WTA main draw when she received a wildcard for Madrid. The 2020 Australian Open junior champion, ranked World No.901, fell to Kiki Bertens in round one.
Martina Hingis holds the record for the most title wins in Tokyo, with five - the last of which came in 2007 when she beat Ivanovic in the final (Getty)
In 2000, Mary Pierce claimed a title on the green clay of Hilton Head before she hoisted the trophy on home soil at Roland Garros.
Serena Williams won her second Charleston title in 2012, dropping just one game as she defeated Lucie Safarova 6-0, 6-1 (Getty)

However, Cincinnati champion Victoria Azarenka was ruthless in dismissing Mertens 6-1, 6-0 to reach her first Grand Slam semifinal since the 2013 US Open - setting up an all-mother rematch of that year's final against Serena Williams.
Simona Halep and Angelique Kerber first met in the final of Doha 2014. The Romanian, then ranked WTA World No.10, came out on top, 6-2, 6-3. (Getty)

cms.title: Venus Williams won her first Dubai trophy in 2010, beating Virginie Razzano in straight sets (Getty)
Venus Williams won her third Dubai title in 2014, beating Alizé Cornet 6-3, 6-0 to extend her winning streak at the event to 15 matches (Getty)
Serena Williams: 2009 Doha - Serena defeated Venus in the WTA Finals’ only all-Williams final to take home the 2009 trophy. (Getty Images)
Martina Hingis lifted the first trophy in Dubai back in 2001 (Getty)
Sara Errani was all smiles in 2016 when she triumphed through a wild week at the Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships for her ninth WTA trophy.

Venus delivered the only bagel set of their rivalry in the round robin stages of the 2008 Doha WTA Finals, triumphing 5-7, 6-1, 6-0 over Serena in the round-robin stages and going on to lift her first trophy at the season-ending championships.

At the 2013 Mutua Madrid Open, the 16 seeds were the Top 16 players in the world, led by reigning champion and World No.1 Serena Williams. The American started her title defense with a first-round win over Yulia Putintseva.
